raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation Add native support for [Wan-Animate-2 Distilled](https://huggingface.co/Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Distilled-Diffusers) (`Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Distilled-Diffusers`), the distilled variant of the 14B character-animation model of the Wan2.2 family. Like the base checkpoint it takes a **reference image** and a **reference video** and produces a clip of the reference subject performing the reference video's motion; the distilled checkpoint does it in 10 steps at `guidance_scale` 1.0 instead of 40 steps with CFG 3.0. Builds on #42941. The distilled checkpoint is served by the same native `WanAnimate2Pipeline`, selected automatically from the checkpoint directory, as configuration on top of the base support: `log_scale = -1.3` in the attention score modifier, 10 steps at `guidance_scale` 1.0, no CFG parallelism, DPM-Solver++ as the [official](https://github.com/Wan-Video/Wan-Animate-2) command-line implementation samples it. ## Modifications ### New - `Wan_Animate_2_14B_Distilled_Config` (`configs/pipeline_configs/wan.py`): the DiT config with `log_scale` -1.3, the official distillation yaml value (a `log_scale` key in the checkpoint's `transformer/config.json` still wins), and `supports_cfg_parallel=False`. `Wan_Animate_2_14B_Distilled_SamplingParam` (`configs/sample/wan.py`): 10 steps, `guidance_scale` 1.0, everything else inherited from the base sampling params. - `WanAnimate2SchedulerLoader`: the distilled checkpoint is sampled with DPM-Solver++ 2M on the Wan sigma grid, like the base checkpoint, because that is what the model authors' command-line implementation runs for both checkpoints (their distilled yaml's `flow_solver: euler` key is read by no code). The `FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler` named in the distilled repo's `scheduler/scheduler_config.json` is read only by the Diffusers pipeline, which also omits the distilled `log_scale` bias. The loader builds DPM-Solver++ for the distilled config without reading that file and loads the checkpoint's `scheduler/` for the base config; it sets `component_names = []` so it stays pipeline-local, like `WanAnimate2TransformerLoader`; the existing loader-registry test covers both. On the same seed DPM-Solver++ lands 1.8 dB closer to the authors' command-line output than Euler on the shipped grid (33.2 against 31.4 dB, at the same cost): the choice matches the authors' executable implementation; it is not a quality ranking. `--scheduler-class-override` is ignored for the distilled checkpoint and one warning says so (the base checkpoint still honours it). - Registry detectors: both repos share the `model_index.json` `_class_name`; the variant is named only by the `_class_name` of `modular_model_index.json`. The distilled detector matches `WanAnimate2DistilledModularPipeline` or a Wan-Animate-2 path whose directory name carries a `distill` token (a token in a parent directory does not count), the base detector the rest, the distilled one registered first because a directory with `model_index.json` matches both through the shared class. `--model-id Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Distilled-Diffusers` pins the variant explicitly. - Cookbook page `docs/cookbook/diffusion/Wan/Wan-Animate-2.mdx`: variant table, defaults note, distilled presets, request examples, the GB200 distilled benchmark section and troubleshooting entries. The command picker config `docs/src/snippets/configs/Wan/wan-animate-2.jsx` gains a **Checkpoint weights** option in the shape of the Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo one (#43391): per-checkpoint defaults and Request command, CFG parallelism disabled, **Auto** topology resolving to Ulysses and **Auto** text encoder to CPU offload for the distilled checkpoint, the nine measured GB200 layouts as verified recipes, covered by `docs/scripts/tests/wan-animate-2-config.test.mjs`. The model catalog lists both ids. - Unit tests in `test/unit/test_wan_animate_2_config.py` (the two configs, the loader, the CFG-parallel rejection, the `guidance_scale` rejection) and routing in `test_registry.py`; the unit tests run offline on CPU. One GPU CI case, `wan2_2_animate_2_14b_distilled_ref2v` (1 GPU, H100): the base case's inputs at the distilled recipe, at the default video consistency thresholds, with a perf scenario. ### Shared code touched - `registry.py`: the modular-index probe, a pure addition. For a local directory that ships `modular_model_index.json`, the detectors are also probed with that file's `_class_name`; unit test in `test_registry.py`. Nothing else outside the Wan-Animate-2 files changes. ### Supported features - Everything the base pipeline supports in #42941 except CFG parallelism: server warmup, Ulysses, TP and TP x Ulysses, text-encoder CPU offload, DiT layerwise offload (never changes a layout's output, about 2 s in the table below), per-request audio, the bf16 DiT with fp32 encoders and VAE. - Server warmup (`--warmup-mode server`, the `sglang serve` default): three synthetic one-clip startup requests with a built-in reference image and a generated silent reference video: the bounded warmup shape, a residency probe at the largest supported budget, 720x1280, that decides whether the DiT stays resident, and the bounded shape again. A request whose frame geometry differs from the warmup shapes pays a one-time flex-attention autotune on its first occurrence (about 16 s on 1 GPU, 12 to 13 s on 2, 9 s on 4); with `--warmup-mode off` or `request` the first real request pays it instead. - Multi-GPU: at `guidance_scale` 1.0 the CFG-parallel auto-enable rule does not fire, so `--num-gpus N` resolves to Ulysses (`--ulysses-degree N`); `--tp-size N` and `--tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2` work as on the base checkpoint. ### Notes on model-specific parameters - The base model's parameters are unchanged (`clip_len`, `fps`, `prompt_ref`, `size` as a pixel-area budget, `video_path` / `video_url`, `seconds` and `num_frames` ignored); The one deviation this PR adds: the distilled checkpoint's scheduler is built in code by `WanAnimate2SchedulerLoader` instead of being read from the checkpoint's `scheduler/`, because the shipped config names a sampler the official reference implementation does not use (see the DPM-Solver++ rationale above). ## Accuracy Tests Inputs of the comparison below, the base PR's inputs, identical for both implementations. | Input 1: reference image (the subject to animate) | Input 2: reference video, 7.9 s at 30 fps (the motion to follow) | | --- | --- | || https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48c9939c-dd47-4800-a3ee-ed635a03eb3f | **Output, side by side:** sglang distilled (this PR) on the left, the official implementation with the distilled yaml on the right, seed 123. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc06693e-466e-4b3b-ae69-6e7bfc9ad718 **Output, frame grid at matching timestamps:** sglang distilled top row, official distilled middle row, official distilled with `log_scale` 0 bottom row. Same inputs in both implementations: a 16:9 reference image and a 7.9 s reference video at 30 fps, `size` 640x800 (a 960x528 frame), `clip_len` 37, 10 steps, `guidance_scale` 1.0, identical prompt and negative prompt, default reference-branch prompt; official = the official implementation with the distilled yaml, 236 aligned frames. sglang vs official is 32.8 dB mean PSNR at seed 123 and 31.9 dB at seed 124, while two seeds of either implementation are about 21 dB apart: the two implementations sample the same point, 11 to 12 dB above the two-seed floor, and the floors coincide. | Pair | PSNR mean / min (dB) | SSIM | LPIPS | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | | sglang vs official, seed 123 | 32.8 / 20.7 | 0.945 | 0.035 | | sglang vs official, seed 124 | 31.9 / 20.6 | 0.940 | 0.038 | | sglang seed 124 vs seed 123 (two-seed floor) | 21.0 / 19.1 | 0.780 | 0.126 | | official seed 124 vs seed 123 (two-seed floor) | 20.9 / 18.9 | 0.755 | 0.128 | | sampler A/B, seed 123: DPM-Solver++ on the official grid (this PR) vs official | 33.2 / 20.6 | 0.948 | - | | sampler A/B, seed 123: Euler on the shipped grid vs official | 31.4 / 20.8 | 0.941 | - | - The official code ran on the same GB200 node in bf16 with torch SDPA in place of flash-attn (the flex-attention path that applies `log_scale` was untouched). The band set before measuring for a same-sample match was 22 to 28 dB; the distilled pairs clear it. The same harness on the base checkpoint (40 steps, CFG 3.0) matched sglang's base output at 20.2 dB mean, the two-seed-floor level; that comparison is not part of this PR. - `log_scale` matters: the official output with `log_scale` 0 is 27.2 dB from its `-1.3` output, and sglang's `-1.3` output is closer to the official `-1.3` output (32.8 dB) than to the official `log_scale`-0 output (26.8 dB). - Sampler A/B at seed 123 (the last two table rows; they use a different frame resize, hence 33.2 against 32.8 dB for the same pair). Rows of the grid: DPM-Solver++ on the official grid (this PR), Euler on the shipped grid, official. - Within sglang: DiT layerwise offload and `sglang generate` are byte-identical to the resident 1-GPU server output, and the second request of every server reproduces the first (same md5). Multi-GPU layouts against 1 GPU with the default encoder and VAE parallel settings, PSNR mean / min dB: Ulysses 2 37.4 / 34.7, TP 2 35.9 / 32.4, Ulysses 4 33.3 / 26.4, TP 2 x Ulysses 2 34.8 / 29.7, TP 4 36.8 / 34.5; layerwise offload never changes a layout's output. - Context only: the distilled 10-step output against the base checkpoint's 40-step CFG-3.0 output on the same seed is 16.7 dB, the base model's two-seed-floor level, i.e. a different sample of the same scene. Base checkpoint at 40 steps (left) against the distilled checkpoint at 10 steps (right), and the grid base-40 / distilled-10 / base at 10 steps and guidance 1.0: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0bfe3c98-5e9f-4840-8517-aa1f2accc226 - CI case on H100: six same-tree generations were bit-identical (`Min SSIM: 1.0000 Min PSNR: inf Max mean_abs_diff: 0.0000`). The case uses the file's video defaults (CLIP 0.90, SSIM 0.92, PSNR 24 dB, mean abs diff 10.0), like the base case. The ground-truth frames are taken from the first CI run. How to run: ```bash # CPU unit tests (configs, loader, routing, CFG-parallel rejection, guidance rejection) pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_wan_animate_2_config.py \ python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_registry.py # GPU CI case (consistency against the H100 ground truth + perf check) pytest -s python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/test_server_1_gpu.py -k wan2_2_animate_2_14b_distilled_ref2v # Serve sglang serve --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Distilled-Diffusers --text-encoder-cpu-offload ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Tested on 1, 2 and 4 GPUs of a 4x GB200 node (189 GB per GPU). Workload: the base PR's workload at the distilled defaults: 10 steps, `guidance_scale` 1.0, fps 30, 237 frames = 7 clips of 37, 640x800 budget on a 16:9 reference image (960x528 frame), seed 123, `sglang serve --text-encoder-cpu-offload --warmup-mode server`, two identical `/v1/videos` requests per server. E2E is the steady state (the second request); peak is the `nvidia-smi` maximum over ranks during the request, in the cookbook's unit (GiB column, `nvidia-smi` MiB / 1000, as the base table reports it). This is the cookbook's distilled GB200 benchmark. | Config | GPUs | Flags (plus `--text-encoder-cpu-offload`) | E2E (s) | Peak per GPU (GiB) | | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | | 1 GPU, DiT resident | 1 | none | 150.2 | 69.5 | | 1 GPU, layerwise DiT offload | 1 | `--dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer` | 150.0 | 39.7 | | 2 GPU, Ulysses2 (framework default) | 2 | `--ulysses-degree 2` | 87.0 | 60.1 | | 2 GPU, Ulysses2, layerwise DiT offload | 2 | `--ulysses-degree 2 --dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer` | 86.3 | 31.4 | | 2 GPU, TP2 | 2 | `--tp-size 2` | 97.1 | 40.0 | | 4 GPU, Ulysses4 (framework default) | 4 | `--ulysses-degree 4` | 55.8 | 51.0 | | 4 GPU, Ulysses4, layerwise DiT offload | 4 | `--ulysses-degree 4 --dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer` | 58.0 | 21.5 | | 4 GPU, TP2 x Ulysses2 | 4 | `--tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2` | 59.3 | 35.3 | | 4 GPU, TP4 | 4 | `--tp-size 4` | 64.1 | 30.4 | Speedups: - Ulysses is the fastest layout, 1.73x over 1 GPU on 2 GPUs (87.0 s vs 150.2 s) and 2.69x on 4 (55.8 s); the tensor-parallel layouts are slower (97.1, 59.3 and 64.1 s). - Layerwise DiT offload costs about 2 s and leaves the output identical while cutting the request-phase peak from 69.5 to 39.7 GiB on 1 GPU, 60.1 to 31.4 GiB on 2 and 51.0 to 21.5 GiB on 4. - The gain over the base checkpoint is structural (4x fewer steps, one branch per step). Every row's first request is 9 to 17 s slower than the steady state: the one-time flex-attention autotune fires because the request's frame geometry differs from the warmup shapes, plus other one-time costs. Whole-run peaks, which include the server warmup's synthetic requests (one at the largest supported budget, 720x1280, to decide whether the DiT stays resident), are higher: 95.5 / 64.8 / 72.3 / 41.9 / 47.3 / 57.4 / 27.3 / 38.9 / 37.8 GiB in row order. - `--enable-torch-compile` on 1 GPU brings no gain: 156.8 s steady state against 150.2 s eager, 1168 s for the first compiled request, 85.9 GiB peak, output 37.5 dB PSNR from eager and identical across requests. ### Recommended parallelism config It is recommended to use `--text-encoder-cpu-offload`. CFG parallelism is rejected for this checkpoint, so every layout below is Ulysses, TP or their combination. **1 GPU** - About 96 GiB or more: defaults (DiT resident): 150.2 s, 69.5 GiB during the request, 95.5 GiB over the whole run including the server warmup's 720x1280 residency probe. - 80 to 96 GB: add `--dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer` (150.0 s, 39.7 GiB during the request, 64.8 GiB over the whole run, identical output). **2 GPUs** - `--ulysses-degree 2` (what `--num-gpus 2` resolves to): 87.0 s, 60.1 GiB per GPU during the request (72.3 GiB whole run). - 80 GB per GPU: the same with `--dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer` (86.3 s, 31.4 GiB during the request, 41.9 GiB whole run, same output), or `--tp-size 2` (97.1 s, 40.0 GiB, 47.3 GiB whole run). **4 GPUs** - `--ulysses-degree 4` (what `--num-gpus 4` resolves to): 2.69x over 1 GPU (55.8 s), 51.0 GiB per GPU during the request (57.4 GiB whole run). - 80 GB per GPU: the same with `--dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer` (58.0 s, 21.5 GiB during the request, 27.3 GiB whole run), or `--tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2` (59.3 s, 35.3 GiB, 38.9 GiB whole run; measured once), or `--tp-size 4` (64.1 s, 30.4 GiB, 37.8 GiB whole run). ## Known limitations and follow-ups - At `guidance_scale` 1.0 the negative prompt is still encoded: the default is a conditioning-cache hit after the warmup, and a custom negative prompt costs one UMT5 forward per distinct value. Skipping it is a follow-up. - CI: ci-data has no ground-truth frames for the distilled case. ## Resolved known limitations - The 720x1280 budget (the official distilled demo default) fails on both checkpoints when the reference image and the reference video have different aspect ratios: each is resized to the requested area at its own ratio and the in-context layout is sized from the image grid only. With the benchmark inputs the image gives 1280x704 = 80x44 = 3520 tokens per frame, the video 1264x720 = 79x45 = 3555, and the reference-video copy overflows (`The expanded size of the tensor (3520) must match the existing size (3555)`). A separate PR sizes the in-context attention slot from the larger of the two grids; until it merges, use 640x800 or crop the reference video to the image's aspect ratio. Everything above runs at 640x800 / `clip_len` 37. Fix in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44090 ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `isort` and `codespell` were run on the touched files; the full pre-commit hook set has not been run.) - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (Unit tests run offline on CPU; the H100 case needs the ci-data frames, see Known limitations.) - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #39280843746](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39280843746) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #39280843598](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39280843598) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #39280843668](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39280843668)

+def _checkpoint_dir(
+    root,
+    *,
+    name: str = "ckpt-7f3a",

+    modular_class: str | None = None,
+) -> str:
+    """Laid out like a published repo: model_index.json, the component folders the index
+    verifier looks for, and modular_model_index.json when a class is given."""
+    ckpt = root / name
+    ckpt.mkdir(parents=True)
+    (ckpt / "transformer").mkdir()
+    (ckpt / "vae").mkdir()
+    index = {"_class_name": index_class, "_diffusers_version": "0.40.0.dev0"}
+    (ckpt / "model_index.json").write_text(json.dumps(index))
+    if modular_class is not None:
+        (ckpt / "modular_model_index.json").write_text(

+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("modular_class", [None, "SomeModularPipeline"])

+    # A checkpoint may ship modular_model_index.json next to model_index.json and name
+    # a finer-grained pipeline there; without it the probes are the path and the
+    # model_index class only.
+    probes = []
+
+    def detector(probe: str) -> bool:
+        probes.append(probe)
+        return False
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(registry, "_MODEL_NAME_DETECTORS", [("probe", detector)])
+    path = _checkpoint_dir(tmp_path, modular_class=modular_class)

+def _load_scheduler(pipeline_config, checkpoint_config: dict | None):
+    """Run WanAnimate2SchedulerLoader with the checkpoint's scheduler_config.json served
+    from memory (None: reading it is an error) and the flag-free server args it reads."""
